learning_objective: The learner will identify eight accessibility features on an illustrated page from a description of how each looks, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** accessibility-page-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify eight accessibility features on an illustrated page from a description of how each looks, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Alt Text, Captions, Transcript, Link Text, Table Accessibility, Keyboard Navigation, Color Independence, Heading Structure (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A video player with a caption button is captioned. (2) The focus ring is a design flaw. (3) A chart is accessible if its colors are bright. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying features on an illustrated page is a Remember-level task that anchors each check to something the learner can look for. The quiz asks the learner to go from the look of a feature to its name. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of a lesson page. At the top is a wide bar of heading text. Below it is a picture with a small tag icon at one corner. A video frame follows, with a strip of thin text lines along its bottom edge and a small badge at the lower right. Under the video is an underlined bar with a small document icon. In the paragraph below, one underlined phrase is set apart. A grid with a shaded top row and a shaded left column follows. A button has a thick outline around it. At the bottom is a bar chart whose bars differ by pattern as well as by shading. The eight markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Descriptive heading | The wide bar of text at the top of the page. | A real heading that names the page, the start of a logical heading structure. | Use one main heading and nest the others in order. | | 2 | Image with alt text | A picture with a small tag icon at one corner. | An image whose purpose is described in its alt text. | Describe the purpose, not just the look. | | 3 | Captioned video | A video frame with a strip of thin text lines along its bottom edge. | A video whose speech appears as timed captions. | Check automatic captions for errors. | | 4 | Transcript link | An underlined bar with a small document icon beneath the video. | A link to a text version of the video's audio and key visuals. | Place it right next to the video. | | 5 | Descriptive link | One underlined phrase set apart inside a paragraph. | A link whose words say where it goes. | Avoid "click here". | | 6 | Table with headers | A grid with a shaded top row and a shaded left column. | A data table whose header cells are marked, so a screen reader pairs each cell with its headings. | Give the table a short caption. | | 7 | Visible focus | A button with a thick outline around it. | The outline shows which control a keyboard user is on. | Never remove the focus outline without a replacement. | | 8 | Chart with patterns | A bar chart whose bars differ by pattern as well as shading. | A chart that does not depend on color alone to tell its bars apart. | Add labels or patterns to any chart that uses color to carry meaning. | **Provenance:** The features follow the chapter sections on alt text, captions, transcripts, link text, table accessibility, keyboard navigation, color independence, and heading structure. The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the page "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 8 in the order of the table. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 8 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can spot an accessible page." Below 7 it lists the labels of the missed features. **Starting State:** The illustration with eight numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what it is." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists these features as checks: headings in order, alt text, captions, a transcript, descriptive link text, table headers, visible keyboard focus, and color independence.
